lxc_ecdd8345d1daf246.text: Puyo is a Japanese puzzle game series where round colored blobs fall, join in groups of four, and pop.

lxc_7bb14d5c95e90ff3.text: Compile made the first game in 1991, Sega took over the series in 1998, and later hits like Puyo Puyo Fever and Puyo Puyo Tetris kept it popular.

lxc_f7d2eb063d2bd71b.text: Puyo is a puzzle game series from Japan.

lxc_9e19d097c1686abb.text: The word Puyo is the name of the pieces.

lxc_f0bae1879321c597.text: A Puyo is a round, soft blob, a little like slime or jelly.

lxc_71ed9571f7cfdd02.text: Each Puyo has a color and a small face, so the game looks cute and bright.

lxc_94db9921ca0c6d16.text: The company Compile made the first games.

lxc_257532222f0ae70c.text: For many years outside Japan, the series had a different name, Puyo Pop.

lxc_94694ff8b06edaac.text: Today the name Puyo Puyo is used everywhere.

lxc_f1d69c78e41a64fb.text: The series is a big success.

lxc_fe4063993c872095.text: Together with the Madō Monogatari games, it has sold more than 10 million copies.

lxc_0364d0350bca3a0d.text: Many people in Japan know the game from game centers, and many first played it at home on a family console.

lxc_497d450cde7c436c.text: Puyo fall from the top of the screen, usually two at a time.

lxc_745a1610dd2e024c.text: You move them left or right, turn them, and drop them.

lxc_001b6cc73a948878.text: When four or more Puyo of the same color touch each other, they pop and disappear.

lxc_df946371b5fae96a.text: They must touch on a side, up, down, left, or right.

lxc_31b17fcea2ab2b41.text: Touching only at a corner does not count.

lxc_fa4ae9b19b0e872e.text: When Puyo pop, the Puyo above them fall down.

lxc_2bd4f97c6e8a3bb5.text: If those falling Puyo make a new group of four, they pop too.

lxc_44fc73d4691c70db.text: A long chain sends garbage to the other player.

lxc_cf241f4d82389936.text: Garbage Puyo, called Ojama in Japanese, are gray blobs that do not pop by themselves.

lxc_342a9a2c3d09ac4d.text: You win when the other player's board fills up to the top of the third column from the left.

lxc_5ec7d7d07f9c16c0.text: The first Puyo Puyo game came out in 1991.

lxc_f8de70e7c1e74f03.text: Compile made it for two Japanese home systems, the MSX2 computer and the Famicom Disk System.

lxc_c49893c874ff8066.text: The characters did not start in Puyo.

lxc_4c0bb60a3f60057d.text: They came from an older Compile game series called Madō Monogatari, also written Madou Monogatari.

lxc_9af7b14d9b4e32f3.text: Madō Monogatari is a role-playing game where you walk through dark dungeons and fight monsters.

lxc_ab8caeeeeded3157.text: Its first game came out in 1990, also on the MSX2.

lxc_714c33ef2c3e3f0d.text: Arle is the main hero of that RPG world.

lxc_b83344862924c9dd.text: She is a young girl who uses magic.

lxc_845e3534c578868d.text: In Puyo Puyo, Arle and the monsters from her world became the players you see on the screen.

lxc_cf9b9ae52156b205.text: So the cute faces on the Puyo and the fighters beside the board all have a story behind them.

lxc_bf89888548a01775.text: In 1992, Compile worked with Sega to bring Puyo Puyo to arcades.

lxc_074b0cc458ea4cff.text: The arcade version ran on Sega's System C2 hardware.

lxc_d7fef8f0dd137c84.text: This version was built for two players who fight each other.

lxc_4b93399eda4d558a.text: The chain rule from Part 2 now became a weapon, because a big chain drops a lot of garbage on your rival.

lxc_4472b6b9bb159273.text: This competitive style was a hit in Japanese game centers.

lxc_2d01f929204cd3e0.text: Sega also sold the game for its home console, the Mega Drive, and many people in Japan bought it.

lxc_6146bbb17b1801db.text: In 1994, Compile released Puyo Puyo 2, called Puyo Puyo Tsū in Japan.

lxc_218bff65ff874cb8.text: It added an important new idea.

lxc_cfe2a361cdc607e9.text: When garbage is coming to you, you can make your own chain and cancel some of it.

lxc_849fefdd253622eb.text: It made matches deeper and faster.

lxc_8617965e17e5a525.text: Compile had money problems in the late 1990s.

lxc_7de4db67cd9da0a5.text: In March 1998, Sega got the rights to Puyo Puyo.

lxc_f2f4d08561f4524e.text: From that time, Sega owned the series.

lxc_d9af0d61f7a49f25.text: After 2001, a Sega team called Sonic Team started to make the new Puyo Puyo games.

lxc_d3cafb710ffaf0d0.text: Sonic Team is famous for the Sonic the Hedgehog games.

lxc_38f4ece66f484635.text: Now the same team made the little blobs too.

lxc_5fd70a7cc9ca0534.text: In 2003 they released a new game.

lxc_03e1028eb18e0955.text: The game was called Puyo Puyo Fever in Japan and Puyo Pop Fever outside Japan.

lxc_bc1d5efc7e5ece96.text: It added a new rule called Fever mode.

lxc_d805b654958c5f56.text: When you counter a lot of garbage, you enter Fever.

lxc_1c88f75c957a5e80.text: The board fills with ready-made chains, and you pop them fast for a short time.

lxc_13adb370db23dd5e.text: The lens from Part 2 still works here.

lxc_cc2602668778a665.text: Pieces fall, colors match, and a big result goes to the other player.

lxc_973a8b92520851e9.text: The series kept going under Sega, and one later game became very famous.

lxc_ec2949300226e66b.text: It is called Puyo Puyo Tetris.

lxc_4ce80c9872de9fae.text: Sega released it in Japan in 2014.

lxc_146711485f0177ea.text: It mixes two big puzzle games in one.

lxc_bf244203a3cb22f3.text: One player can play Puyo Puyo, and the other player can play Tetris at the same time, and they still fight each other.

lxc_0da07cefd57080f0.text: There are also modes where the two games swap during a match, or where Puyo and Tetris blocks fall on the same board.

lxc_07ffe5cf4482d1f8.text: This made the game easy to enjoy with a friend who knows only one of the two games.

lxc_06021429e1c4e2f2.text: Outside Japan, an English version came out in 2017 for the PlayStation 4 and the Nintendo Switch.

lxc_f09cba2fcb0d37ae.text: For many players in Europe and America, this was their first Puyo Puyo game.

lxc_4432a38f72ed7b4a.text: The blobs from a 1991 Japanese computer game now sit next to Tetris on a modern console.
